records.reason: Formal constitutional powers baseline: useful for authority context, but it does not show how Tshisekedi exercised those powers in 2022.
Broad structural assessment of political manipulation and weak institutional independence; useful background, but less direct than incident-level evidence.
Repeats the Kabund arrest already captured more directly in other records without adding a material new fact.
Strong structural media-freedom baseline, but it mostly overlaps with later incident-level reporting and reform claims.
Useful broad rights baseline for the Tshisekedi period, but many of its details are better captured by more direct 2022 incident reports.
Direct, information-rich investigation of martial-law abuses in North Kivu and Ituri; one of the strongest pieces for emergency-rule repression.
Useful institutional background on election-preparation constraints, but it is more general than the later calendar and trust evidence.
Concrete year-end election-calendar milestone with explicit glissement risk; direct evidence on the 2022 electoral timetable.
Same Kabund arrest story as E0060 with less added detail; keep the more information-rich report instead.
Best single Kabund incident account: direct arrest report plus charge language and political context.
Press-freedom violation tally is useful, but it is broadly redundant with RSF, HRW, and the direct reform/repression records.
Strong contemporaneous account of state-of-siege abuse with named victims and specific detention allegations.
Distinct 2022 follow-up showing protest suppression and arbitrary detention under the prolonged state of siege.
Direct presidential ordinance revising emergency jurisdiction; a concrete corrective action and one of the few reform-side records.
Direct presidential commitment on press decriminalization and media independence; a useful reform pledge even though implementation lagged.
Press-law bill adoption overlaps with the press-reform pledge and broader media-freedom evidence without adding much new substance.
Digital-code push is relevant but more peripheral here and largely overlaps with the media-control pattern already covered.
Specific provincial-election irregularity report with concrete bribery allegations; adds a distinct electoral-integrity episode.
Useful trust metric for the CENI and its appointment process, but it measures confidence rather than a direct misconduct incident.
Procedural investiture of opposition CENI members is less informative than the broader election-timetable and trust evidence.
Secondary compilation useful for showing uneven treatment of opposition activity, but it is not a primary incident report.
Specific arrest is useful corroboration, but the chain of responsibility is less direct than the strongest incident-level records.
Concrete military reshuffle is relevant to state control, but it is more about personnel reform than civil political pluralism.

remaining_concerns: Most of the strongest adverse evidence concerns emergency-rule abuse and structural restrictions rather than explicit presidential orders.
Election evidence is strongest on process, timetable, and trust; it does not by itself establish the quality of the final 2023 contest.
The direct 2022 incident record is concentrated in a small number of local or wire-family reports, so corroboration should be carried forward carefully.
